e-4518.problem:
The system of equations

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}6x+4y=1 \\ x-8y-z=-2 \\ 3x+2y-2z=1\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

can be represented using matrix notation as

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14052721/assets/ed434344208758284aa0f144676f7dd6498a63faeb0248d18e87c4be6c3d87f2.png)

What are the values of $a,$ $b$ and $c?$
e-4518.worked_solution:
First, let's write the system so that $x$, $y$, and $z$ appear in each equation:

$$
{\begin{aligned}6x+4y+0z=1 \\ x-8y-z=-2 \\ 3x+2y-2z=1\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can write the system in the form $A\mathbf{x} = \mathbf{b},$ where

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14052721/assets/b9364923447e278db5ec47bef74e1a05310645b30df22d4ea5efcc0de46c6ed2.png)

is the coefficient matrix,

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14052721/assets/16cb1608f70821d138f0c6984038bb42d86d9fbf76d560d94d2e25bd6fdb05e0.png)

is the column vector of constants, and

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14052721/assets/0abbbaf34955fa40d6cdbfa9e16cb1567ee16271d65b4565206a0f2204eedf6d.png)

is the column vector of variables.

So, the equation $A\mathbf{x} = \mathbf{b}$ becomes

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14052721/assets/4b915439c3e9922d692aab4205a728160e0a1286f82fa5ebc736460901581147.png)

Therefore, $a=6,$ $b=2,$ and $c=-2.$

e-4519.problem:
The system of equations

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}2x-y+z=4 \\ z-x+2=-1 \\ 2y-2x-4z=-4\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

can be represented using matrix notation as
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14052721/assets/0d06481c63a618262b9034124c24cd1d0c566ee9d6b891fa470e09dc67f5f6c6.png)
What are the values of $a,$ $b$ and $c?$
e-4519.worked_solution:
First, let's write the system so that $x$, $y$, and $z$ appear in each equation in the correct order and all constants are on the right-hand side of the system:

$$
{\begin{aligned}2x-y+z=4 \\ -x+0y+z=-3 \\ -2x+2y-4z=-4\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can write the system in the form $A\mathbf{x} = \mathbf{b},$ where

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14052721/assets/104c591a6a72cf3caab1bc2a965c57258bb37a31578254696e0c1cd740fe5915.png)

is the coefficient matrix,

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14052721/assets/e008383384401198e67f648cce33a720d98afb6a6f60a14ba7ffa21dcc095a5f.png)

is the column vector of constants, and

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14052721/assets/c85e33202a691b685431ac16efab6a7fd932eac056743df6e81632587f0465b2.png)

is the column vector of variables.

So, the equation $A\mathbf{x} = \mathbf{b}$ becomes

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14052721/assets/64d1f57717dda57c8a7fbc403728ee9699a22ce995f68a50a0b80f25543fdab6.png)

Therefore $a=0,$ $b=-2,$ $c=-3.$

content.problem:
The system of equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}-3x+y+7z=5 \\ x-4y+8z=1 \\ -6y+9z=2\end{aligned}
$$

can be represented using matrix notation as

$$
[\begin{aligned}-3 & 1 & 7 \\ 1 & -4 & b \\ 0 & a & 9\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}c \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].
$$

What are the values of $a,b,$ and $c?$
content.worked_solution:
First, let's write the system so that $x$, $y$, and $z$ appear in each equation:

$$
{\begin{aligned}-3x+y+7z=5 \\ x-4y+8z=1 \\ 0x-6y+9z=2\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can write the system in the form $Ax=b,$ where

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-3 & 1 & 7 \\ 1 & -4 & 8 \\ 0 & -6 & 9\end{aligned}]
$$

is the coefficient matrix,

$$
b=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]
$$

is the column vector of constants, and

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]
$$

is the column vector of variables.

So, the equation $Ax=b$ becomes

$$
[\begin{aligned}-3 & 1 & 7 \\ 1 & -4 & 8 \\ 0 & -6 & 9\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, $a=-6,\,b=8,\,c=5.$

after.name: Question 2
after.problem:
The system of equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}3x-4y+z=2 \\ x-6y+11z=3 \\ 3x-4y-z=4\end{aligned}
$$

can be represented using matrix notation as

$$
[\begin{aligned}3 & -4 & a \\ 1 & b & c \\ 3 & -4 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3 \\ 4\end{aligned}].
$$

What are the values of $a,b$ and $c?$
after.worked_solution:
We can write the system in the form $Ax=b,$ where

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}3 & -4 & 1 \\ 1 & -6 & 11 \\ 3 & -4 & -1\end{aligned}]
$$

is the coefficient matrix,

$$
b=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3 \\ 4\end{aligned}]
$$

is the column vector of constants, and

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]
$$

is the column vector of variables.

So, the equation $Ax=b$ becomes

$$
[\begin{aligned}3 & -4 & 1 \\ 1 & -6 & 11 \\ 3 & -4 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3 \\ 4\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, $a=1,\,b=-6,\,c=11.$

content.problem:
The system of equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}2x-5y+z=1 \\ -x-3y+9z=-2 \\ 4x-7y-z=5\end{aligned}
$$

can be represented using matrix notation as

$$
[\begin{aligned}2 & -5 & c \\ -1 & b & 9 \\ a & -7 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ 5\end{aligned}].
$$

What are the values of $a,b$ and $c?$
content.worked_solution:
We can write the system in the form $Ax=b,$ where

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & -5 & 1 \\ -1 & -3 & 9 \\ 4 & -7 & -1\end{aligned}]
$$

is the coefficient matrix,

$$
b=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ 5\end{aligned}]
$$

is the column vector of constants, and

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]
$$

is the column vector of variables.

So, the equation $Ax=b$ becomes

$$
[\begin{aligned}2 & -5 & 1 \\ 1 & -3 & 9 \\ 4 & -7 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ 5\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, $a=4,\,b=-3,\,c=1.$

after.problem:
The system of equations

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}-2x+y+z=-1 \\ z+3x-2y=3 \\ -y+2z-x=-4\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

can be represented using matrix notation as

$$
[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 & 1 \\ 3 & b & 1 \\ -1 & -1 & c\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}a \\ 3 \\ -4\end{aligned}].
$$

What are the values of $a,b$ and $c?$
after.worked_solution:
First, let's write the system so that $x$, $y$, and $z$ appear in each equation in the correct order and all constants are on the right-hand side of the system:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}-2x+y+z=-1 \\ 3x-2y+z=3 \\ -x-y+2z=-4\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can write the system in the form $Ax=b,$ where

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 & 1 \\ 3 & -2 & 1 \\ -1 & -1 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$

is the coefficient matrix,

$$
b=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 3 \\ -4\end{aligned}]
$$

is the column vector of constants, and

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]
$$

is the column vector of variables.

So, the equation $Ax=b$ becomes

$$
[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 & 1 \\ 3 & -2 & 1 \\ -1 & -1 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 3 \\ -4\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, $a=-1,\,b=-2,\,c=2.$

content.knowledge_point: Identifying Entries of a Matrix Product Representing a 3x3 System of Equations by Reorganizing
content.problem:
The system of equations

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}-2x+y+z=-1 \\ z+3x-2y=3 \\ -y+2z-x=-4\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

can be represented using matrix notation as

$$
[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 & 1 \\ 3 & b & 1 \\ -1 & -1 & c\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}a \\ 3 \\ -4\end{aligned}].
$$

What are the values of $a,b$ and $c?$
content.worked_solution:
First, let's write the system so that $x$, $y$, and $z$ appear in each equation in the correct order and all constants are on the right-hand side of the system:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}-2x+y+z=-1 \\ 3x-2y+z=3 \\ -x-y+2z=-4\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can write the system in the form $Ax=b,$ where

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 & 1 \\ 3 & -2 & 1 \\ -1 & -1 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$

is the coefficient matrix,

$$
b=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 3 \\ -4\end{aligned}]
$$

is the column vector of constants, and

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]
$$

is the column vector of variables.

So, the equation $Ax=b$ becomes

$$
[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 & 1 \\ 3 & -2 & 1 \\ -1 & -1 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 3 \\ -4\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, $a=-1,\,b=-2,\,c=2.$

after.name: Question 8
after.problem:
The system of equations

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}5y-3z+x=2 \\ 3z+7x-2y=5 \\ 2x-2y=-1\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

can be represented using matrix notation as

$$
[\begin{aligned}a & 5 & -3 \\ 7 & b & 3 \\ 2 & -2 & c\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 5 \\ -1\end{aligned}].
$$

What are the values of $a,b$ and $c?$
after.worked_solution:
First, let's write the system so that $x$, $y$, and $z$ appear in each equation in the correct order and all constants are on the right-hand side of the system:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}x+5y-3z=2 \\ 7x-2y+3z=5 \\ 2x-2y+0z=-1\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can write the system in the form $Ax=b,$ where

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 5 & -3 \\ 7 & -2 & 3 \\ 2 & -2 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

is the coefficient matrix,

$$
b=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 5 \\ -1\end{aligned}]
$$

is the column vector of constants, and

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]
$$

is the column vector of variables.

So, the equation $Ax=b$ becomes

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 5 & -3 \\ 7 & -2 & 3 \\ 2 & -2 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 5 \\ -1\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, $a=1,\,b=-2,\,c=0.$

content.problem:
The system of equations

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}2y+5x=3z+2 \\ 3x-6y=5 \\ 2x-3y+5z=-1\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

can be represented using matrix notation as

$$
[\begin{aligned}5 & a & -3 \\ 3 & -6 & b \\ 2 & c & 5\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 5 \\ -1\end{aligned}].
$$

What are the values of $a,b$ and $c?$
content.worked_solution:
First, let's write the system so that $x$, $y$, and $z$ appear in each equation in the correct order and all constants are on the right-hand side of the system:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}5x+2y-3z=2 \\ 3x-6y+0z=5 \\ 2x-3y+5z=-1\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can write the system in the form $Ax=b,$ where

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}5 & 2 & -3 \\ 3 & -6 & 0 \\ 2 & -3 & 5\end{aligned}]
$$

is the coefficient matrix,

$$
b=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 5 \\ -1\end{aligned}]
$$

is the column vector of constants, and

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]
$$

is the column vector of variables.

So, the equation $Ax=b$ becomes

$$
[\begin{aligned}5 & 2 & -3 \\ 3 & -6 & 0 \\ 2 & -3 & 5\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 5 \\ -1\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, $a=2,\,b=0,\,c=-3.$

after.problem:
The system of equations

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}-2z+x-5y=1 \\ -y+5z-4x=-2 \\ 2x-6y-z=2\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

can be represented using matrix notation as

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & -5 & a \\ b & -1 & 5 \\ 2 & c & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ 2\end{aligned}].
$$

What are the values of $a,b$ and $c?$
after.worked_solution:
First, let's write the system so that $x$, $y$, and $z$ appear in each equation in the correct order and all constants are on the right-hand side of the system:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}x-5y-2z=1 \\ -4x-y+5z=-2 \\ 2x-6y-z=2\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can write the system in the form $Ax=b,$ where

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & -5 & -2 \\ -4 & -1 & 5 \\ 2 & -6 & -1\end{aligned}]
$$

is the coefficient matrix,

$$
b=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]
$$

is the column vector of constants, and

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]
$$

is the column vector of variables.

So, the equation $Ax=b$ becomes

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & -5 & -2 \\ -4 & -1 & 5 \\ 2 & -6 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, $a=-2,\,b=-4,\,c=-6.$
